decisions.quote: A series of five experiments replicated the results obtained by Aviezer et al. (2012; Experiment 1) and extended them to other tasks (i.e., affective priming, affective misattribution procedure, feeling, and action tendencies). The results show that stimuli presenting only bodies, rather than faces, consistently produce these classic effects found in the literature.

shipped.title_o: Body Cues, Not Facial Expressions, Discriminate Between Intense Positive and Negative Emotions
shipped.outcome_quote: A series of five experiments replicated the results obtained by Aviezer et al. (2012; Experiment 1) and extended them to other tasks...The results partially confirm this objective. We observed the effect on the valence dimension reported by Aviezer et al.: Images representing only bodies or bodies with faces produced stronger valence effects than images representing only faces. However, unlike Aviezer et al., we observed a valence effect in the face condition. In contrast, we did not replicate the arousal effect observed by Aviezer et al. (2012). We found that images of bodies and faces or bodies alone were rated as inducing higher semantical arousal than images of faces alone. Overall, our results are consistent with Aviezer et al. (2012; Experiment 1).
